statement: The supplied sources do not contain a derivation of Principal Component Analysis: the expected derivation using Lagrange multipliers, quadratic form differentiation, or SVD factorization is entirely absent from the supplied text, and the covariance derivation section is incomplete and truncated mid-sentence ('Hence (*) holds if and only if cov(X)'). Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is defined as an orthogonal linear dimensionality reduction technique that transforms a centered data matrix B = X - h u^T of size n x p into a lower-dimensional projection T = B W of size n x L (where 1 <= L <= p), or y = W_L^T x (equivalently Y = KLT{X}), where W consists of the first L columns of the eigenvector matrix V that diagonalizes the empirical covariance matrix C = (1 / (n - 1)) B^* B such that V^{-1} C V = D, with D being a diagonal matrix of eigenvalues sorted in decreasing order (D_{kk} = lambda_k) and V containing the corresponding orthonormal eigenvectors.

properties.property: For any orthonormal linear transformation y = B' x, tr(Sigma_y) is maximized by taking B = A_q, where A_q consists of the first q columns of the eigenvector matrix A.
properties.why: the first q principal components capture the maximal cumulative variance among all q-dimensional orthogonal projections

properties.property: For an orthonormal transformation y = B' x, tr(Sigma_y) is minimized by taking B = A_q^*, where A_q^* consists of the last q columns of A.
properties.why: the trailing components have minimal variance and detect near-constant linear relationships or outliers

properties.property: The covariance matrix admits the spectral decomposition Sigma = sum_{k=1}^p lambda_k alpha_k alpha_k', decomposing total variance into Var(x_j) = sum_{k=1}^p lambda_k alpha_{kj}^2.
properties.why: orthonormal eigenvectors decouple the covariance matrix into ranked non-increasing variance contributions

properties.property: Assuming zero mean and unitary P, cov(PX) = P cov(X) P^{-1}, diagonalizing the output covariance when P aligns with the eigenvectors of cov(X).
properties.why: orthonormal transformation into the eigenspace of cov(X) renders distinct components pairwise uncorrelated

properties.property: Under additive Gaussian signal s and i.i.d. Gaussian noise n, the projection y = W_L^T x maximizes mutual information I(y; s) and minimizes information loss I(x; s) - I(y; s).
properties.why: PCA achieves information-theoretic optimality for linear dimensionality reduction under Gaussian noise models

properties.property: A PCA based on the correlation matrix of X is identical to a PCA based on the covariance matrix of standardized variables Z.
properties.why: correlations are covariances of normalized variables that have already been mean-centered and scaled to unit variance

assumptions.assumption: Linearity of data relationships: features exhibit linear correlations and can be effectively represented by an orthogonal linear coordinate rotation.
assumptions.breaks_when: The underlying data manifold has hidden nonlinear patterns, causing PCA to fail to capture the true structure or misdirect analysis.

assumptions.assumption: Mean-centering: the dataset centroid is translated to the origin prior to covariance computation (B = X - h u^T).
assumptions.breaks_when: Mean subtraction is omitted on raw unstandardized data, causing the rank-one term n mu mu^T to dominate the leading eigenvector toward the mean rather than the true variance axes.

assumptions.assumption: Commensurate feature scaling: variables are measured on comparable units or standardized to unit variance.
assumptions.breaks_when: Features have disparate units (e.g., temperature and mass) or unstandardized variances, causing principal components to arbitrarily rotate toward columns with inflated variance.

assumptions.assumption: Noise independence and Gaussianity for information optimality: additive noise is independent, identically distributed, and Gaussian.
assumptions.breaks_when: Noise components become dependent or correlated, causing PCA to lose its information-theoretic optimality.

assumptions.assumption: Sample size adequacy and lack of serial correlation: sufficient sample observations (n >= 30) without unhandled autocorrelation.
assumptions.breaks_when: Sample size is small (n < 30) or serial correlation is uncorrected, introducing severe sampling bias into estimated principal components beyond the first.

assumptions.assumption: Sign neutrality: the data domain admits negative values created during mean-removal.
assumptions.breaks_when: Physical quantities are strictly non-negative (such as astrophysical flux exposures), where mean removal produces unphysical negative values.

failure_modes.signature: Leading principal components align almost exclusively with individual variables that have numerically large variances or units.
failure_modes.cause: Applying PCA directly to unstandardized covariance matrices when variables possess different measurement scales or inflated variances.

failure_modes.mode: Centroid domination from omitted mean subtraction
failure_modes.signature: The first principal component points directly toward the empirical mean vector mu rather than the direction of maximal spread.
failure_modes.cause: Diagonalizing the uncentered scatter matrix Sigma_unc where the rank-one term n mu mu^T obliterates centered covariance structure.

failure_modes.signature: Low explained cumulative energy across components and poor representation of obvious geometric patterns in the data.
failure_modes.cause: PCA relies entirely on linear transformations and cannot capture nonlinear dependencies or curved manifolds.

failure_modes.mode: Unphysical negative values in non-negative data
failure_modes.signature: Reconstructed signals exhibit negative values where physical quantities must be strictly non-negative.
failure_modes.cause: Mean subtraction forces the sample mean to zero, creating negative values in strictly non-negative physical signals (e.g., astronomy).

failure_modes.mode: Loss of information optimality under dependent noise
failure_modes.signature: Suboptimal mutual information preservation and elevated information loss between the source signal and reduced representation.
failure_modes.cause: Violation of the i.i.d. noise assumption where noise covariance contains off-diagonal dependence.

failure_modes.mode: Sampling error and serial correlation bias
failure_modes.signature: Substantial distortion and bias in the orientation and ordering of components beyond the first principal component.
failure_modes.cause: Small sample size (n < 30) or unhandled autocorrelation structure among sequential data observations.

failure_modes.mode: Poor class discrimination in pattern recognition
failure_modes.signature: Heavy overlap between classes in the reduced principal component space despite high total variance explained.
failure_modes.cause: PCA optimizes total unsupervised variance rather than class separability (unlike linear discriminant analysis).
